source.title: Understanding the Emergence of Seemingly Useless Features in Next-Token Predictors
source.authors: Mark Rofin; Jalal Naghiyev; Michael Hahn

page_placements.theme: Where features useless for the next token come from: retention for later positions vs circuit sharing

record.tranche_reason: The study measures pre-caching and its relationship to future-token look-ahead, and concludes that pre-cached features are not the source of look-ahead in Gemma 2; it also reports settings where pre-caching does and does not contribute to feature learning.
record.gate_note: The paper also discusses prior work on future-token prediction, but cited results are not recorded as rows. The Gemma steering results were induced by feature steering and do not directly test the claim versions. Results about syntax, Othello, and toy tasks are included where they measure feature learning or pre-caching.
record.test_reason: The study uses Wu et al.'s myopic training plus its own gradient-path attribution to test whether models compute features for later positions (V3), in toy tasks, Othello and TinyStories. In Gemma 2 2B it tests whether pre-cached features drive future-token decodability. It concludes they do not, and argues for the breadcrumbs account (V6). Its results also argue that V3's scope must be restated: pre-caching matters for some features but not for syntax or look-ahead.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but incomplete. The authors conclude that seemingly NTP-useless features emerge through pre-cached and shared (circuit-sharing) gradient paths. They find pre-caching is needed for coherent TinyStories generation and for multi-layer toy circuits, but not for syntax. In Gemma 2, features with extreme pre-caching degree relate to code and formal structure. Pre-cached features contribute less to linear look-ahead than direct features. They call this strong evidence for the breadcrumbs account rather than implicit planning.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses training-gradient decomposition and ablation, plus SAE-feature interventions and feature-to-readout alignment. It does not reproduce the original rhyme-planning intervention or directly test whether changing candidate future tokens changes intervening text.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported contribution of pre-caching varies by feature type: it is important for the TinyStories positional feature but much smaller than direct influence for POS and dependency features. The look-ahead analysis varies token distance from t+1 through t+5 and readout-subspace rank.

fits_no_version.finding: In OthelloGPT, shared (circuit-sharing) gradients give positive training signal to NTP-useless board squares. This is separate from pre-caching. In Conditioned Majority, the tied model seems to learn a shortcut driven by shared gradients.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Features that look NTP-useless can arise through parameter sharing across positions (circuit sharing), not only through pre-caching or next-token use.

record.problems: The Gemma 2 analysis estimates influence near the final checkpoint rather than along training, and the paper notes that the look-ahead result is a feature-alignment analysis. The plotted look-ahead correlations have no exact values stated in the text. The paper also says Othello influence results are noisy and non-stationary across positions.
record.rows_left_out: The induced Gemma feature-steering generation results are omitted because they measure behavior under deliberate steering, not naturally occurring look-ahead or pre-caching. The general Othello probe-performance comparisons are omitted because they do not separately measure pre-cached influence.

untested.parts: All of it: no rhyming verse, no frontier model, no rhyme-word intervention.
Linear future-token readouts are trained for Gemma 2 2B, but their prediction accuracy is never reported.
All of it: no rhyme planning in open models.
All of it. Othello is studied for world-model features, not look-ahead; there is no chess, Sokoban or multi-step reasoning task.
How far ahead plans reach is not measured. Steering of generation by a plan is not tested; the Gemma analysis is feature–readout alignment only, at layer 15 with one SAE.
In Gemma, Q(w) is estimated only around the final checkpoint, not along training. Pre-caching is not tested in verse or planning tasks.

missing.what: Majority accuracy under myopic training: tied 1.00 ± 0.00, 10-untied 0.96 ± 0.05. Myopic models can solve a task that needs no multi-layer pre-cached circuit. This is the control contrasting with R5–R6.
Myopic OthelloGPT trains unstably and does not reach non-myopic loss or accuracy (Figure 9).
Pearson correlations between readout alignment and Q(w) lie within about ±0.02, i.e. near zero. This bears on how strong the negative-correlation evidence is.
Layer-wise Wilcoxon results for the positional feature. Pre-cached exceeds direct in layers 2–3 (p 1.4e-7, 1.1e-5). Direct exceeds pre-cached in layer 1 (p 4.5e-8).

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for any version. The 'strong evidence' wording for breadcrumbs rests on small correlations from one SAE at one layer. Steering results (Figure 19, Table 6) are induced and were rightly left out. In R17–R21, distance labels follow the paper's t, where the target is position i+t+1.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming-verse task, candidate rhyme-word representation, or intervention changing a rhyme ending is tested.
The study trains future-token readouts, but reports feature-to-readout alignment correlations rather than whether a single hidden state predicts tokens several positions ahead with stated accuracy.

The study does not test whether the features shape intermediate text in rhyming verse or other generation tasks; its large-model analysis estimates influence around the final checkpoint, not across the full training trajectory.
No open-weight rhyme-planning mechanism or open attribution-graph rhyme analysis is tested.
No multi-step reasoning, chess, or Sokoban look-ahead behavior is tested.
Look-ahead is analyzed only for Gemma 2 2B and distances t+1 through t+5; the paper does not test the listed reasoning, chess, or Sokoban tasks.

relationships.condition: Small trained Transformers: Conditioned Majority toy task, OthelloGPT NTP-useless squares, TinyStories loss and positional feature
relationships.reason: Myopic models fail Conditioned Majority (0.76 vs 0.99/1.00) and have higher TinyStories loss (3.29 vs 2.53). Pre-cached influence is positive for NTP-useless Othello squares, and exceeds direct influence for the positional feature in middle layers (R1, R2, R5, R6, R8, R10, R14).
relationships.display_finding: Myopic models achieved 0.76 versus 0.99/1.00 on Conditioned Majority and incurred TinyStories loss of 3.29 versus 2.53, while influence through later positions was positive for next-token-irrelevant Othello squares and exceeded direct influence for middle-layer positional features.

relationships.display_finding: Across look-ahead maps extending up to 5 extra tokens, pre-caching correlated weakly and negatively with future-token alignment, with Pearson correlations near zero.

relation.reason: Its own training ablations, gradient decomposition and SAE experiments bear directly on pre-caching and incidental look-ahead.

tranche.reason: The study explicitly argues that pre-caching does not exclusively explain look-ahead and offers feature-specific qualifications alongside positive pre-caching results.

source_check.notes: The study does steer SAE features and measure code/punctuation generation; causal steering of look-ahead readout directions is untested. Cross-study counts and comparisons were assessed only for claims about this study.

statements.correction: High-Q features have lower look-ahead readout alignment; pre-cached features contribute less than direct features according to the authors; correlations do not establish zero contribution or training origins of readout information.
statements.problem: The opening claim excludes any contribution from pre-cached features; the text says they contribute less than direct features. This also tests an explanation of decodability rather than establishing a limitation of V3 itself.

statements.correction: Figure legends t+1 through t+5 correspond to t=1 through 5 in target i+t+1: two through six tokens ahead.
statements.problem: The distance ambiguity can be resolved from the predictor equation; the plot legends are not literal distances of one through five tokens.

statements.correction: V3 is supported by training ablations, gradient decomposition and local Q estimates; syntax qualifies its feature scope. Look-ahead alignment supports the authors' V6 interpretation without showing that V3 fails.
statements.problem: The reported facts are supported, but treating the look-ahead alignment result as a V3 limitation adds a requirement absent from V3.
